# Vendored microReticulum

Generated by `scripts/vendor_microreticulum.py`; do not edit files here by hand.
Change the script or `patches/microreticulum/overlay/` and regenerate. This
README is part of the overlay, and the script refuses to run unless it lists
every pin the script uses.

## Exclusions

`main.cpp`, `Provisioning`, the TLSF allocator, `greatest.h`, heatshrink's
Graphviz state diagrams, `CBC` and every microStore adapter except the POSIX
one. See `EXCLUDED` in the script.

## Changes on top of upstream

The two forks are upstream plus the commits below and nothing else. Each fork
commit is open upstream except where noted; once they merge, the pins can move
back to upstream.

microReticulum: fork of upstream `40fa628809d57140180c1c833559ab96fec992c1`.

| Fork commit | Change | Upstream |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `e36c727` | `OS::sleep()` uses `usleep()`: ESP-IDF has no `nanosleep()` | [#97](https://github.com/attermann/microReticulum/pull/97) |
| `c6c5c75` | Path and known-destination stores open without transport enabled, so a leaf node can keep paths and announces | [#75](https://github.com/attermann/microReticulum/pull/75) (someone else's, the same fix) |
| `37098e0` | Link proofs are validated; the check was stubbed to false, so no packet sent over a link was ever proven | [#99](https://github.com/attermann/microReticulum/pull/99) |
| `5b15c9b` | `teardown()` on a closed link returns early, rather than firing the closed callback again | [#100](https://github.com/attermann/microReticulum/pull/100) |
| `40e02c4` | The link watchdog, ported from the Python reference: keepalives, stale and timed-out links | [#101](https://github.com/attermann/microReticulum/pull/101) |
| `1e37e64` | Receipt timeouts run after the job loop, so a timeout callback that sends does not wait on itself | [#102](https://github.com/attermann/microReticulum/pull/102) |
| `eab6361` | `Destination::set_default_app_data()`, so a path response carries the LXMF announce data | fork PR #7; upstream #104 proposes the same method |
| `f84ac91` | A single-packet request response is passed through as raw msgpack, which LXMF propagation-node collection needs | fork PR #8; not yet proposed |
| `dc46747` | `Token` and `Fernet` refuse a token without at least one whole block of ciphertext, PKCS#7 unpadding checks the pad length, and padding fills every byte with it. A 48-byte token with a valid HMAC read past an empty buffer, so one packet to any announced destination crashed the node | fork PR #9; to propose |
| `cebcff7` | `Resource::accept()` rejects an advertisement whose transfer size is zero or larger than one encrypted segment (`Type::Resource::MAX_TRANSFER_SIZE`, which `RNS_RESOURCE_MAX_TRANSFER_SIZE` can lower) before allocating. The receiver sized its parts and hashmap from the claimed size, so one advertisement could make it allocate as much as the sender liked | fork PR #10; to propose |

microStore: fork of upstream `0f28567fe00ab8ab14624a34c2e9e0a000a44c46`.

| Fork commit | Change | Upstream |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0e9a523` | `rmdir()` in the POSIX and stdio adapters returns true on success, as `mkdir()` does | [#12](https://github.com/attermann/microStore/pull/12) |
| `6f0c4e0` | The POSIX adapter resolves paths against its base path and keeps its own copy of it; ESP-IDF has no working directory | [#13](https://github.com/attermann/microStore/pull/13) |

## SolarOS overlay

`patches/microreticulum/overlay/` replaces these files after the trees are
copied. Nothing else in this directory differs from the pinned revisions.

| File | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `microReticulum/Cryptography/Hashes.cpp` | SHA-256 and SHA-512 on mbedtls |
| `microReticulum/Cryptography/HMAC.h` | HMAC on mbedtls; upstream's free-digest path feeds the digest twice |
| `microReticulum/Cryptography/HKDF.cpp` | HKDF over the HMAC above; upstream ignores the context argument |
| `microReticulum/Cryptography/AES.h` | AES-CBC on mbedtls |
| `microReticulum/Cryptography/Ed25519.h` | Ed25519 on the orlp code SolarOS already carries for MeshCore (`src/vendor/meshcore/ed25519`), with input sizes checked |
| `microReticulum/Cryptography/X25519.h` | X25519 on the reference code in `components/wireguard_lwip`, with input sizes checked |
| `microReticulum/Cryptography/Random.h` | Every random byte from the ESP32 hardware RNG (`esp_fill_random()`); upstream's `randomnum` has 8 bits of entropy per call |
| `RNG.h` | Nothing to seed or service, in place of rweather's software RNG |
| `microReticulum/Utilities/Memory.{h,cpp}` | No TLSF pools: containers use `operator new`, heap statistics come from `heap_caps_*` |
| `microReticulum.h` | The umbrella header without Provisioning, which is not vendored |

## Integration requirements

- `CONFIG_COMPILER_CXX_EXCEPTIONS=y` (the library throws).
- `USTORE_USE_UNIVERSALFS=1`, `RNS_USE_FS=1`, defined by the build that compiles
  the library; this tree alone builds nothing.
- The X25519 overlay uses `crypto/refc/x25519.h` from SolarOS's
  `components/wireguard_lwip`, so the compiling component must require it.
- `esp_fill_random()` is a true random source only while Wi-Fi or Bluetooth is
  on, or inside `bootloader_random_enable()`. Identity and link keys must be
  made under one of those.
- Set `RNS_RESOURCE_MAX_TRANSFER_SIZE` to the largest resource segment the
  integration takes. The default, one 16 MiB segment, is more than a small
  device can hold.
- The FAT mount must allow at least 8 open files: each store keeps an index and an
  active segment open, plus one transient descriptor per read.

## Known upstream defects (0.5.0)

The overlay replaces the code with the first four; the last is still there.

- `Random.h` `randomnum` yields 8 bits of entropy per call.
- The HMAC free-digest path feeds the digest twice.
- HKDF ignores its context argument.
- Ed25519/X25519 input sizes are not checked.
- A repeated announce from a known destination does not refresh its stored app data.
